QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_6

question.text: An SROI ratio of 0.85:1 computed by Mr. Arjun Desai (SIA) on a livelihood program indicates:

answer.text: The SIA cannot issue an opinion because SROI ratios below 1 are inadmissible under SAS-100
For every INR 1 of social value, INR 0.85 of investment was made — the program is highly efficient
The deadweight is 85% — the assumption set must be rejected
For every INR 1 invested, INR 0.85 of social value was created — i.e., the program destroyed net social value relative to investment and is not positive

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SROI = monetised Impact Value / Investment. A ratio of 0.85:1 means every INR 1 invested generated only INR 0.85 of social value — the program did NOT achieve a positive net return on social investment. ≥1:1 is the generally accepted threshold for positive social return. **The Trap:** Option 2 inverts the ratio. Option 3 confuses SROI with deadweight %. Option 4 is false — SAS-100 does not bar SIAs from reporting sub-1 ratios; the ratio still gets reported with appropriate qualitative narrative. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A Distributor discusses return ratios for MF schemes — XXIII applies analogous arithmetic to social outcomes. X-A IA mentions benefit-cost ratios. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** If you compute SROI<1, do not suppress it — report the ratio plus a narrative on deadweight, assumption sensitivity, and whether drop-off over longer horizons would eventually push it above 1. Transparency is your shield.
